notes from /dev/null
by Charles Choi ìµë¯¼ì
Take Two: Eshell
30 Jun 2025  Charles Choi
This is a contribution to the
Emacs Carnival 2025-06: Take Two
collection of posts on Christian Tietzeâs blog.
My first take with
Eshell
many years back did not leave a good impression. My early expectations was that it should act like any other shell, only to be unpleasantly surprised by it. It took a long time for me to warm up to Eshell. Upon reflection, it was because I wasnât ready for it.
Now Eshell is an inseparable part of my Emacs experience. Paradoxically though, I find little occasion to use Eshell in the same way Iâve used shells in the past. Much of what I used to use the shell for, I do today with Emacs modes instead.
It was not always this way. Like so many users who started Unix computing in the 80âs, I started with the command line (for myself
ksh
and later
bash
), studiously internalizing command line tools and their arcane syntaxes to support file management, running programs, and systems administration. Overwhelmingly though, it was file management and running programs that I did through the command line.
For file management these days,
Dired
is my interface of choice. It is simply the more elegant tool for the job.
Case in point: renaming a bunch of files in a directory to arbitrary names. With a shell, my standard approach would have been to run some variant of
ls -1 > foo.sh
, edit
foo.sh
to insert
mv
on each line to a renamed target file,
chmod u+x foo.sh
to be executable, run
foo.sh
, delete
foo.sh
and call it a day.
With Dired, the above steps are replaced as such: make the buffer writable (via
Wdired
). Change the target filenames to a desired result, then commit the changes. This is even easier if there is a pattern you can use a regexp for. Unsurprisingly, all the basic file management operations that you would want are supported by Dired. Add
Casual Dired
to help make these operations discoverable and youâll soon consider how quaint using
mv
,
cp
,
rm
, and
ls
are.
Running a simple command on a file? Again, you can do that with Dired. Move the point to the Dired line containing the file. Type â!â and enter a command in the prompt. You can optionally reference the filename in the command with the â?â character if you want to redirect its output to a file (e.g.
cmd ? > outfile
).
Taking file management and running simple commands out of what you would use a shell for, whatâs left over? Source code management (SCM)?
Like for many others,
git
is my goto tool for SCM.  Much has been said about the terrible user experience of the
git
command line and for years I suffered with its design decisions. Thankfully for Emacs users, there is Magit and VC mode which both provide a saner experience for it.
Running a Makefile? Use Emacs
compile
, which provides command completion for the targets defined in the Makefile and error/warning navigation if needed. (Try out
Casual Make
for editing Makefiles in Emacs.)
Do you need to run a command with arcane arguments repeatedly? Again, Makefile +
compile
to the rescue where it can be used as a task runner for that command.
Need robust terminal emulation? Eshell will fail you here and you are likely better off using a dedicated terminal emulator app, separate from Emacs. That said, Iâve found the built-in
term
to be good enough for many curses-style utilities.
Mining data files with piped commands? Eshell is a power tool here: used wrongly and you could figuratively cut off a limb. But used cleverly, Eshell offers great value. More on this later.
So with all these use cases described, why even use Eshell?
Using Eshell becomes a win only if you know
Elisp
. With that, you can think of Eshell as an Elisp REPL that can secondarily act as a shell.
Letâs not mince words. For many users this is a high bar, as it takes into account
a lot
of prerequisite knowledge. That said, learning basic Elisp is trivial for readers already conversant with programming and manageable for those that arenât. Personally, I was very late (decades!) in taking the time to learn Elisp because I didnât see the reward in it and so, prioritized accordingly. That hesitancy turned out to be unfounded. Elisp is easy to learn and the reward (or punishment) for knowing it is having the ability to really
use
the full capabilities of Emacs. (Know Python? Hereâs a
cheatsheat for Elisp
that I wrote, hop in, the waterâs fineâ¦)
Once gained, bringing Elisp knowledge to using Eshell gives you a command line super power: the ability to improvise shell commands with Elisp functions.
Consider the following Eshell example where we wish to apply a command on a set of
png
files in a directory. Letâs start with a simple example that simply echoes filenames with suffix
.png
.
$
for
i
in
*.png
{
echo
$i
}
In Eshell, you can replace
echo $i
with an Elisp expression.
$
for
i
in
*.png
{
(
format
"%s"
i
)
}
You can also mix shell commands and Elisp via
dollar ($) expansion
. Note that

data.title: Development of a transputer ISA board
data.author: nanochess
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在1993-1996年间开发transputer软件的经历，以及近期用JavaScript编写transputer模拟器的过程。作者为了在PC上运行旧软件，设计了一个与Inmos B004兼容的ISA接口板，并从eBay购买了transputer板。作者详细描述了ISA板的设计和制作过程，包括使用TTL电路设计解码原理图、焊接组件时遇到的问题以及如何解决噪声问题。最终，作者成功运行了1993年的Pascal编译器和光线追踪软件。随后，作者学习了KiCAD 9设计软件，创建了新的原理图并尝试使用自动布线工具。尽管遇到一些困难，作者最终完成了ISA板的设计和制作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Toledo的PCB设计文章及相关技术选择的讨论，涉及具体元件选择、PCB设计工具的使用、Transputer架构的优势和限制，以及对传统技术的怀旧。

不同观点：
• Kragen对文章中使用74LS00系列而非74HCT00系列表示疑问，质疑这是出于怀旧还是实际需求，并探讨了TTL与TTL兼容的CMOS之间的差异。他提到不确定ISA是否需要TTL电平，并对元件选择表示好奇。
• MeteorMarc对Kragen提到的KiCAD中的自动布线功能表示感谢，并分享了手动布线的局限性，特别是在原理图需要更改时，手动布线的体验不如自动布线便捷。
• Librasteve讨论了Transputer架构（特别是occam编程语言）相对于现代CUDA和SIMD架构的优势，提出利用现代工艺可以制造出更高效的Transputer阵列，但指出热量问题是主要挑战。
• Taid9iK对Transputer和Occam技术表达了怀旧情绪，回忆了相关的编程结构如SEQ、PAR、CHAN等，并表示这些技术曾给他带来心灵上的平静。
• Webdevver则从怀旧角度提出希望恢复传统的CPU地址/数据总线设计，希望在现代PCI上实现类似功能，并表达了对通过低级编程控制硬件的兴趣。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于为何选择74LS00系列元件，Kragen认为可能是出于怀旧，而实际应用中74HCT00可能更合适。
• 讨论还涉及Transputer架构在现代工艺下的潜在性能优势，librasteve提出了非常具体的计算和预测，但同时承认热量管理是重大挑战。
• 怀旧情绪贯穿多个评论，taid9iK和webdevver都提到了对过去技术的怀念，尽管他们的具体关注点不同。

Development of a transputer ISA board
I developed software for transputers in the years 1993-1996. A few months ago, I wrote some articles about my experiences, and most recently I developed a
transputer emulator in Javascript
.
After my transputer emulator in Javascript was working, I got curious about running my software on a PC computer. I have several PC motherboards with ISA connectors, and I decided to build a card compatible with the Inmos B004 (a single board to test transputer processors). Out of curiosity, I decided for compatibility because I wanted to run the Inmos Occam compiler.
A quick look in eBay and I got two transputer boards (TRAMs) for $25 each one. Both based on the Inmos T805 transputer running at 30 mhz.
I got the port numbers for the board from
Geekdot
, and designed a decoder schematic based on TTL circuits.
My first schematic for the board.
The TRAM board contains the transputer and its memory. It is connected to the ISA board with an Inmos C011 chip that serializes and deserializes the communication link. This chip is accessed via the ports 0150H-0153H. My ISA board also provides a 5 mhz oscillator, two flip-flops to reset and analyse the transputer, and a tri-state gate to read the error status.
Ports of an Inmos B004 board
Offset
Field
0150H Read
Receive data
0151H Write
Send data
0152H Read
Receive status
0153H Read
Send status
0160H Write
Latch bit 0 = Direct to Reset
0161H Write
Latch bit 0 = Direct to Analyse
0160H Read
Bit 0 = Direct from notError
I required a single ISA board drilled for homebrew development. I was going to buy one board in eBay for $35 dollars shipped, but I considered it was way too expensive. After some searching, I found the PCBWay showcase, where this same board was available for sale. And better, I could get 5 boards of 10x10cm. for $25 dollars shipped.
The ISA board for homebrewing.
I got the board and I started to put sockets for the chips. It took me a while to get the oscillator working. Once it was generating the 5 mhz. clock, I wired everything step-by-step, testing as possible. I was so happy doing this, that I never noticed I built the components on the solder side. My first insertion on a PC motherboard killed two 74LS08 when I feed 12V+ through the chips, until I realized my board was backwards.
My board also has a lot of noise produced by the wiring. After adding some decoupling capacitors, I was able to run
my Pascal compiler and ray tracing software from 1993
.
The transputer board working with the ray tracer. Notice my wrong mounting side, and that I'm using an AMD K5 motherboard.
The ISA board I've built.
Going the PCB route
A few weeks later, I decided to learn a little about KiCAD 9, so I installed it on my Macbook Air. Having used OrCAD many years ago, and my own programs that I developed later (I need to write more about it), I recognized most of the tools, and fortunately for this article, KiCAD comes with a predesigned ISA bus component.
Once I put the ISA bus component on the sheet, I wondered if there was a 74LS245 in the library, and yes, so I started adding the components. I wired the pins. I also used the component designer to create the Inmos C011 chip, and the TRAM pinout.
In less than two hours I had a schematic for my transputer board. It looked good, and from some tutorials in Youtube I heard about a very easy path from schematic to printed circuit board, so I exported the netlist, solved some bugs, and then invoked the PCB program. I discovered that I was missing the footprint for the TRAM.
With the footprint designed, the components appeared almost magically in the workspace. And you only had to click and drag and drop the components to their place! This was heaven! I didn't found an autorouter, so I went ahead to draw some lines.
I had worked five hours already, and I was pretty bored because I had to redraw line after line to make space in the board, or basically every time some line crossed the wrong place and it blocked other lines. I had heard of an autorouter for KiCAD, but it required to install Java (I remember in the 2010s I avoided as possible the slow and weird Oracle's installer), but I couldn't find a way to tell KiCAD I had downloaded an autorouter.
It happens KiCAD has gone through so many iterations that there are tutorials since KiCAD 6. I was reading the information for the wrong version. In KiCAD 9 you only need to open the complements window from the initial startup window, select Freerouter, and you need also to install a more compact Java version called Eclipse Temurin.
The autorouter didn't worked in the first attempt, because my board outline was open somehow. After some work I was able to make the outline in a single polygon. I made sure the design rules check (DRC) were correct, with some further work going back to the schematic to tag the unused lines, and correct the voltage lines.

data.title: BYD Seal 06 DM-i Variant: 2,000 Kilometer Range at USD15,340
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary:
BYD推出了Seal 6 DM-1车型，这是一款4.8米长的插电式混合动力旅行车，最高续航达2000公里。车内可容纳5名乘客，储物空间达670升，后座放倒后可增至1535升。该车提供三种配置，起价15,320美元，搭载10 kWh电池。基本款采用1.5升自然吸气发动机与120 kWh电动机，8.7秒内可加速至100公里/小时，纯电续航约80公里，油耗为3.15升/100公里（约74英里/加仑）。更高配置版本采用160 kWh电动机和18.7 kWh电池，纯电续航提升至150公里，油耗为4.25升/100公里（约55英里/加仑）。

该车配备12.8英寸屏幕、8.8英寸液晶仪表盘、六个扬声器、六个安全气囊、LED头灯以及加热通风前排座椅。还搭载BYD的DiPilot 100驾驶辅助系统，可在高速公路上自动导航。高配版配有15.6英寸屏幕、八个扬声器和七安全气囊，并采用DiSus-C阻尼系统提升舒适性。

BYD推出这款旅行车主要是出于对空气动力学效率的考虑，尽管SUV更受欢迎，但旅行车在能效上更具优势。

6th July 2025, 12:53 am
BYD keeps flooding the zone with new models. It now has a plug-in vehicle for just about every price range and keeps adding more. The latest goodie from Shenzhen is the Seal 6 DM-1 Variant, a 4.8 meter (16 foot) long plug-in hybrid wagon with up to 2000 km (1240 mi) of total range using the generous Chinese standard.
Inside, the BYD Seal 6 DM-1 can carry 5 passengers with 670 liters (23 cu ft) of room for their stuff. With the rear seat folded, cargo capacity jumps to 1535 liters (54 cu ft). To put that into perspective, the Chevy Equinox EV has 26.4 cubic feet of cargo room with the second row seatback up and 57.2 cubic feet with it down. The car will be available in three trim levels, starting at $15,320 with a 10 kWh battery.
The fifth-generation BYD plug-in hybrid system has a 1.5 liter naturally aspirated engine with 74 kW (99 hp) that is paired with a 120 kW (161 hp) electric motor. It can reach 100 km/h in 8.7 seconds and uses 3.15 liters of fuel every 100 km, which translates to about 74 mpg. Battery only range is about 80 km (50 mi).
A second powertrain option uses the same engine but adds a more powerful 160 kW (215 hp) electric motor and an 18.7 kWh battery. That combination slices a full second off the 0 to 100 km/h run and increases the battery-only range to about 150 km (90 mi). The BYD Blade battery can be charged from 30 to 80 percent in 25 minutes. Because this version is heavier, its fuel consumption is 4.25 liters per 100 km, or about 55 mpg. Those numbers would probably be about a third lower in the EPA rating scheme, but that’s irrelevant since this car is never coming to the US.
BYD Seal 6 DM-1 Specs
According to
Car News China
, the BYD Seal 6 DM-1 Variant comes standard with a 12.8-inch screen, an 8.8-inch LCD instrument cluster, six speakers, six airbags, LED headlights, plus heated and ventilated front seats. It is also equipped with BYD’s
God’s Eye C
— otherwise known as DiPilot 100 — drive assistance system, which uses 12 cameras, 5 mm wave radars, and 12 ultrasonic radars. The “100” number indicates the system’s computing power in trillion operations per second (TOPS). God’s Eye C is capable of navigating on autopilot on limited-access highways.
In top of the line trim, the BYD Seal 06 DM-i Variant comes with a larger 15.6 inch screen, eight speakers, and seven airbags. It is also equipped with the BYD DiSus-C damping system that enhances riding comfort with fast-acting solenoid valves that adjust in milliseconds to changing road conditions.
Prices for the BYD Seal 06 DM-i Variant are as follows:
BYD Seal 06 DM-i wagon 80 km Noble — 109,800 yuan ($15,320)
BYD Seal 06 DM-i wagon 150 km Exclusive — 119,800 yuan ($16,720)
BYD Seal 06 DM-i wagon 150 km Flagship — 129,800 yuan (18,115 )
Thoughts On Variants
There was a time when every suburban home in America had a station wagon parked in the driveway. They were just production sedans with the roof extended backwards to the rear bumper and were fantastic for carpools and hauling stuff from Point A to Point B. The tradition dates back to the iconic Ford “woodie” so popular with surfers before the Volkswagen Transporter came along.
Some called these cars beach wagons, others called them ranch wagons, but they were all really large vehicles that could swallow enormous amounts of stuff or sleep two on blowup mattresses. American Motors started the trend for “fold back seats” immortalized by
Carly Simon as she sang about
her former lover camping out “by the lakes and forests” with his new squeeze.
Such vehicles are sometimes called a “shooting brake” in Jollye Olde Englande or a “variant” on the Continent. America’s love affair with the station wagon has waned over the years, replaced first by minivans and later by SUV lust. Personally, I was always smitten with the assortment of midsize wagons from Volvo, Volkswagen, and BMW. For a while, I thought my perfect car would be a Volkswagen Passat TDI wagon with a 6-speed transmission. I was actively searching for one when the news about Dieselgate broke.
The BYD Seal 6 DM-1 is really a derivation of those iconic American wagons, like the Ford LTD Country Squire, which was really just an extended roof version of the LTD sedan. The DM-1 is just an extended roof version of the Seal 6 sedan.
Why a wagon? That’s an interesting question. They are virtually nonexistent in the US, but have a loyal following in Europe. In China, most customers prefer an SUV, so why is BYD putting resources into the wagon version of the Seal 6? The answer, in a word, is aerodynamics. A wagon is a little slipperier than an SUV. In the world of EVs — which includes plug-in hybrids — aerodynamic efficiency is a critical consideration.

data.title: Mirage: AI-native UGC game engine powered by real-time world model
data.author: zhitinghu
data.article_summary: Mirage是一款由AI驱动的实时生成游戏引擎，允许玩家通过自然语言、键盘或控制器输入，即时创建和修改游戏世界。与传统预设关卡的游戏不同，Mirage支持动态、互动和持续的游戏体验，玩家可以随时生成新的游戏内容，如城市小巷、载具或扩展城市天际线。该引擎突破了以往生成技术的限制，提供更高画质、更长互动体验，并且支持多种游戏类型，如《GTA》风格的《Urban Chaos》和《Forza Horizon》风格的《Coastal Drift》。Mirage标志着UGC 2.0时代的到来，玩家可以创造、演变和重塑独特的游戏体验，而不再受限于预设脚本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成游戏世界的现状与未来潜力

不同观点：
• Peritract：认为当前技术并没有真正的持久世界模型，声称其为“世界模型”言过其实，只是现有游戏的模糊复制品，尽管技术有趣，但宣传过度。
• ilaksh：持乐观态度，认为尽管目前技术不完善，但与过去视频生成模型的发展类似，随着更多训练和优化，未来可能实现通过提示生成游戏，类似于当前生成视频或代码的能力，甚至可能应用到生产力工具上。
• abrookewood：对UGC（用户生成内容）不了解，认为当前示例类似于AI生成的Quake demo，缺乏实际的世界，只是过去游戏的“幽灵”再现。
• motoxpro：从趣味性和新奇体验角度看待当前技术，认为虽然不符合传统游戏标准，但提供了独特的体验，有其价值。
• samrus：提出两个问题，一是缺乏内在逻辑一致性，难以达到如《Skyrim》或《New Vegas》的深度互动；二是数据同质化问题，担忧AI生成内容可能导致市场饱和，抑制原创游戏开发。
• gausswho：持怀疑态度，认为相关讨论多为炒作。
• bakugo：批评当前demo只是GTA IV游戏视频的拼接，缺乏真正的创新。
• lianhuiqin：对未来充满期待，想象一个每个人都能创造、游玩和分享自己游戏的未来。
• zhenwang9102：对技术方向感到兴奋，认为上传图片生成游戏世界类似于《Ready Player One》中的OASIS，尽管目前仍粗糙，但未来可期。
• joechenphd：分享具体示例，强调通过上传图片生成互动游戏世界的酷炫功能。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于当前AI生成游戏世界的真实性和潜力。一部分人认为技术尚不成熟，宣传过度，另一部分人则看好其未来发展，认为随着技术进步可能带来革命性变化。
• 数据同质化和市场饱和是另一个值得注意的讨论点，特别是对原创游戏开发的潜在影响。
• 不同评论者对新技术的趣味性和新奇体验有不同看法，有的重视其即时娱乐价值，有的则关注其长期影响和艺术深度。

Play Demo: Urban Chaos (GTA-style)
Play Demo: Coastal drift (Forza Horizon-style)
The future of gaming isn't built level by level by expert designers—it's imagined, generated, and played by
anyone, in real time.
Meet
Mirage
: the world's first real-time generative engine enabling live UGC gameplay through
state-of-the-art AI World Models. Built to support dynamic, interactive, and sustained gameplay, it enables
entire worlds to be generated and modified live—through natural language, keyboard, or controller input.
Mirage supports various genres, and today we are releasing two playable demos:
Urban
chaos (GTA-style)
and
Coastal drift (Forza Horizon-style)
—both are fully generated on the fly. These aren't scripted experiences; they're living,
playable simulations shaped in real time by each player.
Mirage sits at the cutting edge of AI. Compared to recent works, such as AI Doom and Genie from Google, AI
Minecraft from
Decart, and AI Quake II from Microsoft, Mirage offers several distinct advantages:
It enables user-generated content (UGC) through text input at any moment during gameplay-marking a
significant leap beyond previous world-model-based game generation approaches.
It produces more photorealistic visuals, moving beyond the pixelated or blocky styles in earlier
systems.
It supports much longer interactive experiences, with playable sequences extending beyond ten minutes.
While
Mirage still has its limitations—as you may notice in the demos—we're confident that as we continue to push the
frontiers of real-time generative technology, it will play a defining role in the future of gaming.
UGC 2.0: The Rise of Generative Play
Traditional games are pre-authored: the city is laid out, missions are scripted, and the experience is
ultimately finite. Mirage breaks this boundary by letting players create new experiences dynamically as they
play.
Using natural language, keyboard input, or controller actions, players will be able to request an alley to
escape through,
spawn a vehicle, or expand the city skyline on the fly. The game responds instantly, weaving these
user-generated elements seamlessly into the ongoing simulation. The world isn't just interactive—it's
co-evolving with the player.
Mirage can generate games in various genres—from racing to RPGs to platformers:
◀
▶
This is
UGC 2.0
:
Where anyone can generate their own games from just a text prompt
Where players create, evolve, and reshape the game live as they play
And where every experience is unique, dynamic, and never pre-scripted
Built on Next-Gen AI
Mirage is powered by cutting-edge World Model research, featuring a large-scale, transformer-based
autoregressive
diffusion model capable of generating controllable, high-fidelity video game sequences. This
technology
framework integrates several key innovations:
A Foundation Trained on Games
Mirage is built on a robust training foundation designed for understanding and generating rich gaming
experiences. This foundation begins with the large-scale collection of diverse game data from across the
internet—providing the breadth needed to capture a wide array of game mechanics and styles.
To complement this, we built a specialized data recording tool that captures high-quality, human-recorded
gameplay interactions. These curated sessions enrich the dataset with nuanced, high-fidelity examples crucial
for training a model to grasp intricate player behaviors and contextual game logic.
The collected and recorded data is then fed into a vertical training pipeline—a domain-specific training
approach focused on games. This allows the model to deeply internalize game world rules, systemic patterns,
and interactive dynamics.
The result is a model capable of generating coherent, realistic, and flexible game content, moving beyond the
constraints of traditional, pre-authored games.
Interactive Generation Meets Real-Time Control
Mirage redefines real-time interaction by integrating frame-level prompt processing into its core. This
enables players to input commands or prompts that are immediately interpreted in the context of ongoing
gameplay.
Playable anywhere via cloud gaming:
Dynamic Input System: Mirage processes player input—primarily via keyboard and text—with ultra-low latency
for near-instant response.
Real-Time Output: Visual updates are streamed back to the browser through a full-duplex communication
pipeline, where input and output flow in parallel, eliminating lag and ensuring fluid interaction.
Under the hood, Mirage is powered by a customized causal Transformer model, augmented with:
Specialized visual encoders
Revised positional encoding
A structure optimized for extended interactive sequences
Borrowing from both LLMs and diffusion models, Mirage supports coherent, high-quality content generation. We
applied an advanced distillation strategy to the diffusion component that ensures both speed and quality.
Players can reshape the environment at any time using natural language, triggering instant world up

主要讨论点：对某个硬件项目的技术实现和可行性的分析，包括FPGA的应用和SMD手工焊接的难度。

不同观点：
• [Neywiny的观点]：Neywiny认为在这个项目中使用FPGA是一个很好的选择。他建议FPGA可以通过PCIe接口实现160个UARTs，但质疑7系列FPGA的I/O能力，认为可能需要等待Spartan US+系列发布。同时，Neywiny对IO电平问题表示担忧，显示出对该方案的部分不确定性。

• [Rochus的观点]：Rochus关注的重点在手工焊接SMD元件的难度。他对项目中有人能够在如此大规模下手工焊接SMD元件表示惊叹，特别是还进行了电路板修正。Rochus称赞了此人的视力和手工的稳定性，强调了这一技术活的高要求。

补充讨论：

A few months ago, I needed to send an email. But when I opened Microsoft Outlook, something had changed.
Microsoft asked me to use Copilot to write my email. Copilot is my AI
companion
. (That’s the cute word they use.)
Hey I don’t want a
companion
—especially not a fake AI buddy. I never asked for this.
And what about the people receiving my emails? They don’t want this either. They want to hear from me, not a bot.
How do I turn my
companion
off?
Please support my work by taking out a premium subscription—for just $6 per month (even less if you sign up for a year).
Subscribe
After some trial-and-error, I found a way to disable Copilot. Phew!
But a few days later, Microsoft surprised me again. It wouldn’t let me save an Excel file until I had agreed to new terms for my software account.
Guess what? AI is now bundled into
all
of my Microsoft software.
Even worse, Microsoft recently
raised the price of its subscriptions by $3 per month
to cover the additional AI benefits. I get to use my AI companion 60 times per month as part of the deal.
Source
But I don’t want to use it. I want to
kill
it.
As you can see, I’ve never used this service. I still have all 60 credits unused. But I’m paying for it—because it’s now embedded into Microsoft Word, Excel, etc.
This is how AI gets introduced to the marketplace—by force-feeding the public. And they’re doing this for a very good reason.
Most people won’t pay for AI voluntarily—just 8%
according to a recent survey
. So they need to bundle it with some other essential product.
You never get to decide.
Source
Before proceeding let me ask a simple question: Has there ever been a major innovation that helped society, but only 8% of the public would pay for it?
That’s never happened before in human history. Everybody wanted electricity in their homes. Everybody wanted a radio. Everybody wanted a phone. Everybody wanted a refrigerator. Everybody wanted a TV set. Everybody wanted the Internet.
They wanted it. They paid for it. They enjoyed it.
AI isn’t like that. People distrust it or even hate it—and more so with each passing month. So the purveyors must bundle it into current offerings, and force usage that way.
“That’s the blight of the AI revolution. It looks like spam. It smells like spam. It tastes like spam.”
There’s another reason why huge tech companies do this—but they don’t like to talk about it. If they bundle AI into other products and services, they can
hide the losses
on their income statement.
That wouldn’t be possible if they charged for AI as a standalone product. That would make its profitability (or, more likely, loss) very easy to measure.
Shareholders would complain. Stock prices would drop. Companies would be forced to address customer concerns.
But if AI is bundled into existing businesses, Silicon Valley CEOs can pretend that AI is a moneymaker, even if the public is lukewarm or hostile.
It’s like a restaurant selling granite rocks for dessert. Nobody will buy them or eat them—so the product fails miserably. But if a popular restaurant adds a dollar to the meal price, and gives every customer a rock with their bill—well, then they can say that:
Every customer gets rocks for dessert.
Every customer pays for it.
Their business is more profitable because of the tasty granite rocks.
This is how AI accounting works in Silicon Valley.
“The AI business model would collapse overnight if they needed consumer opt-in. Just pass that law, and see how quickly the bots disappear. ”
And that’s why Google does something similar to Microsoft. They add AI to search results—you don’t get to choose. It’s force-feeding all over again.
So these huge digital platforms can pretend that users have totally embraced the new tech.
Shut up, buddy, and chew on your rock
.
This is how AI gets implemented
everywhere
.
You don’t get to choose. You’re never asked. It just shows up. Now you have to deal with it.
I don’t want AI customer service—but I don’t get a choice.
I don’t want AI responses to my Google searches—but I don’t get a choice.
I don’t want AI integrated into my software—but I don’t get a choice.
I don’t want AI sending me emails—but I don’t get a choice.
I don’t want AI music on Spotify—but I don’t get a choice.
I don’t want AI books on Amazon—but I don’t get a choice.
If they gave people a choice, they would reject this tyranny masquerading as innovation.
The AI business model would collapse overnight if they needed consumer opt-in.
Just pass that law, and see how quickly the bots disappear.

data.title: OBBB signed: Reinstates immediate expensing for U.S.-based R&D
data.author: tareqak
data.article_summary: 2025年7月3日，美国众议院通过了参议院版本的《一个大美法案》（OBBBA），对联邦税收政策进行了重大改革。新法恢复了100%的额外折旧，立即为美国国内研发费用提供全额支出，终止了多项《通胀削减法案》（IRA）的清洁能源计划，并永久延长了个税减免。同时，为中产阶级家庭和制造商引入新的激励措施。具体亮点包括：恢复100%额外折旧，为制造业提供特别折旧优惠，国内研发费用可立即扣除，终止多项绿色税收抵免，并增加第179条的支出上限。此外，州和地方税（SALT）扣除上限提高，国际税收改革收紧，低收入住房税收抵免（LIHTC）上限增加，支持经济适用房建设。总体而言，该法案旨在促进国内生产和亲商业活动。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国税法第174条变化对研发费用和软件开发支出的影响，以及其对就业、外包、企业决策等方面的潜在后果。

不同观点：
• **对第174条修改的正面评价**：一些评论认为恢复对研发费用的即时支出是积极的变化，原本就不应该修改这一规定。这将有助于创新企业改善现金流，尤其是小型软件企业。有人预期这将促进软件开发就业的增长。（@tomrod, @johncole）

• **对外包和工资差异的影响**：有观点指出，尽管15年的研发费用摊销规则对税收有影响，但由于国外工资水平远低于美国（通常低50-70%），企业仍会选择外包以节省成本。因此，税收上的不利影响被工资差额所抵消，企业仍然会继续外包研发工作。（@me551ah）

• **对法案整体的批评和质疑**：一些评论对美国立法过程的效率和合理性提出质疑，认为法案常常包含到期规则或延迟实施，导致不确定性。这种立法方式可能会对企业和员工产生负面影响。还有人将当前情况与更广泛的政治和经济问题联系起来，质疑国家的治理能力。（@pavlov, @agwa）

• **对就业影响的讨论**：部分评论关注这一税法变化是否会导致之前因税法修改而失去的岗位回归。有人持怀疑态度，认为即便税法调整，其他因素（如AI和利率）仍可能导致进一步的裁员。（@jofzar, @phtrivier）

• **国际对比和其他国家的激励措施**：有评论提到其他国家（如加拿大）对研发费用的激励政策更为慷慨，这可能使美国企业在国际竞争中处于不利地位。这种对比引发了对美国研发补贴政策的讨论。（@ttul）

补充讨论：
• **法案的其他影响**：有评论指出该法案还涉及其他领域的变化，如对赌博损失扣除的限制，显示出法案内容的广泛性和随机性。（@charlieyu1）

• **关于企业预期的讨论**：有人提到在法案通过前，一些企业可能已经根据预期调整了招聘策略，例如更多地指定“仅限美国远程”的职位。这表明税法变化对企业决策的潜在影响。（@rwallace）

争议焦点：
• **法案的实际效果**：对于该法案是否能真正恢复因税法修改而失去的岗位，评论中存在不同看法。有人期望就业增长，有人则认为其他经济因素将继续影响就业市场。

Breaking News – July 3, 2025
Today, the House passed the Senate’s version of the “One Big Beautiful Bill Act” (OBBBA),
marking a significant overhaul to federal tax policy. The signing reflects a major pivot in legislative priorities toward domestic production and pro-business tax policy.
The new law restores 100% bonus depreciation, reinstates immediate expensing for U.S.-based R&D, terminates dozens of Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) clean energy programs, and permanently extends individual tax cuts. It also introduces fresh incentives for middle-class families and manufacturers with details outlined below.
Latest Tax Highlights
100% Bonus Depreciation Restored
Businesses can immediately expense qualifying assets placed in service after January 19, 2025, eliminating the previously scheduled phase-down. This change is expected to drive accelerated capital investment across industries.
New Bonus Depreciation for Manufacturing QPP (Section 168(n))
Qualified production property enjoys 100% bonus depreciation until 2029, a significant benefit for domestic manufacturers and supply-chain operators.
Immediate Expensing of U.S. R&D (Section 174 Rule Fixed)
Domestic research costs are now fully deductible under new Section 174A. Foreign R&D must still be amortized over 15 years. Companies with capitalized domestic R&D expenses from 2022–2024 can elect a catch-up deduction, which could significantly improve cash flow for firms engaged in innovation.  Additionally, eligible small businesses may elect to retroactively apply full expensing to tax years beginning after 2021, allowing them to amend prior returns and recover previously amortized costs.
IRA Clean Energy Incentives Terminated
The law eliminates many IRA-era green tax credits, including 179D, 45L, and electric vehicle credits. 179D terminates for properties
beginning construction after June 30, 2026
. 45L terminates for all dwelling units that are
closed or initially leased after June 30, 2026.
This reversal requires developers and energy companies to revisit project economics for renewable energy initiatives.
Curtailment of Clean Energy ITC and PTC (48/45)
Projects relying on the Investment Tax Credit (ITC) under Section 48 and the Production Tax Credit (PTC) under Section 45 must begin construction within 12 months of the date of enactment of this Act to qualify. Projects placed in service after December 31, 2027, are no longer eligible for these credits. The Act also terminates the tech-neutral credits under Sections 48E and 45Y for electricity production through wind and solar facilities, effectively shifting incentives away from long-term clean energy projects.
Additional Tax Highlights
Section 179 Expensing Cap Increased:
Small businesses can expense up to $2.5 million in qualifying property, creating an expanded opportunity for equipment-heavy operations to write-off costs. The phase-out threshold also rises to $4 million, enabling more businesses to take full advantage of these deductions
SALT Work-Arounds Preserved:
The final text retains full deductibility of state and local taxes paid through state-enacted pass-through entity taxes in over 30 states, a critical win for real estate partnerships and other pass-through businesses.
SALT Cap Increased with Phaseout for High Earners:
The $10,000 cap on state and local tax deductions has been raised to $40,000 for most taxpayers. However, the benefit phases out for households with adjusted gross income (AGI) exceeding $500,000, tapering to restore the lower cap for high earners.
Section 899 “Retaliatory Tax” Eliminated:
The updated text fully drops the controversial Section 899 retaliation measures that would have chilled foreign investment in United States real estate
Excess Business Losses Softened:
The revised text drops plans to permanently silo active pass-through losses from wages and investment income, preserving flexibility for business owners.
Section 163(j) Business Interest Deduction Changes:
Revised EBITDA-based limitation supports capital-intensive businesses and improves access to financing for growth-oriented firms.
International Tax Reforms:

• **对法案整体的批评和质疑**：一些评论对美国立法过程的效率和合理性提出质疑，认为法案常常包含到期规则或延迟实施，导致不确定性。这种立法方式可能会对企业和员工产生负面影响。还有人将当前情况与更广泛的政治和经济问题联系起来，质疑国家的治理能力。（@pavlov, @agwa）

• **对就业影响的讨论**：部分评论关注这一税法变化是否会导致之前因税法修改而失去的岗位回归。有人持怀疑态度，认为即便税法调整，其他因素（如AI和利率）仍可能导致进一步的裁员。（@jofzar, @phtrivier）

• **国际对比和其他国家的激励措施**：有评论提到其他国家（如加拿大）对研发费用的激励政策更为慷慨，这可能使美国企业在国际竞争中处于不利地位。这种对比引发了对美国研发补贴政策的讨论。（@ttul）

• **法案的其他影响**：有评论指出该法案还涉及其他领域的变化，如对赌博损失扣除的限制，显示出法案内容的广泛性和随机性。（@charlieyu1）

• **法案的实际效果**：对于该法案是否能真正恢复因税法修改而失去的岗位，评论中存在不同看法。有人期望就业增长，有人则认为其他经济因素将继续影响就业市场。

data.title: Overthinking GIS (2024)
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了在现代地图制作中，地理信息系统（GIS）如何提供了海量且详细的数据，尤其是公共可访问的地图网站。作者希望通过GIS数据定义一个更人性化的“可用性”指标，具体是指地形是否适合建设。为此，作者试图计算地形的坡度（grade），因为靠近的等高线表示陡峭地形，而距离较远则表示平坦地形。

作者下载了USGS提供的高分辨率数字高程模型（DEM）数据，并使用数学方法如梯度和拉普拉斯算子来计算地形的坡度变化。通过这些计算，作者能够以量化方式评估地形的“可用性”，并通过编程工具（如OpenCV和NumPy）实现这一过程。文章强调了从GIS数据中提取更有意义信息的复杂性，以及使用数学和编程进行数据处理的重要性。

44478861.article_content:
Overthinking GIS
15/7/2024
7-minute read
A roundabout way to downsampling data
Maps in the Modern Era
GIS is probably one of the best things to happen to cartography in the last couple hundred years.  I say that with absolutely no knowledge of the history of map making, but GIS is wildly useful and consistent in how it is presented on publicly-accessible sites.  I can go to the
USGS National Map Viewer
and am presented with more data and information than I could possibly ever find useful.
Even more surprising is that county-level GIS websites look similar enough to the national map and other county maps that someone just roughly familiar with GIS and layers can find more granular information about a single parcel of land.  Personally I don’t have a use for a color-coded sale year plot, but this county in Georgia provides it.  The breadth and depth of information to the general public is incredible.
Custom Metrics
Still though, all of this information is quantifiable because computers don’t speak human languages (LLMs are still
just
math) and what I wanted is something more human-centric, more qualitative: usability.  I’m defining usability as “not too steep to build on” which sounds straightforward until you actually try to come up with a number that defines that.  The closest thing to my usability metric is
grade
and while the USGS map provides elevation and topographic information it does not tell me the grade, at least I couldn’t find that option in the layers.  If a GIS wizard out there wants to point me in the direction of a grade map it would make my life a lot easier.
I decided to define usability as the average grade for some area of land. Ok, great, but how do I calculate that with the data on hand?  The USGS map provides topographic lines, and past experience reading topo maps has taught me what “too steep” is, but that’s the result of over a decade of hiking and reading maps.  How do I tell the computer “when you see topo lines close together it’s
probably
too steep and has a low usability score”?.
In this section of map the grade on the Western side of the river is too steep to use, but the flat area on the Eastern side is perfect.  Topo lines close to each other indicate steep terrain, and lines far apart indicate flatter terrain.
Source Data
Topo maps are available for download from the USGS site, but that’s just a map and isn’t very useful to the computer.  I suppose using
thresholding
I could select only the topo lines but that still doesn’t give me the usability score I want.  Digging deeper, the topo maps are derived from elevation data and that is also available to download.  Multiple sources and derived products are available, and I chose the highest resolution data offered which is the DEM source in ~3m resolution.
I verified the resolution with
gdalinfo
looking at
Pixel Size
:
$ gdalinfo steep_north_tile.tif | grep Pixel
Pixel Size = (3.125000000000000,-3.125000000000000)
Calculating Usability
With the source data downloaded it was time come up with a calculation for my usability metric.  As I said earlier the closest common value to what I want is grade.  Grade can be defined as “rise over run” or $y=mx + b$ where $b$ is 0 and we don’t really care what $y$ is.  The value we care about is $x$, the slope of the terrain. This works for a 1D case but I want to take into account slope in two directions so we have to move up from middle school math to calculus, specifically vector calculus.  In vector calculus the
gradient
describes the rate of change of a function in multiple directions (dimenions) and is just the partial derivative of a function for a given direction.  If I have some function that describes how how the land is shaped and I wanted to find the rate of change (grade) in the $x$ direction I would calculate the partial derivative of the function with respect to $x$, and similarly for $y$. The first derivative gives us the slope, and the second derivative gives us the rate of change of the slope.
This rate of change of slope is “how close are the topo lines?” described mathematically.
Glossing over a lot of details, there is a mathematical operator called the
Laplacian
that calculates the second order differential for a scalar field.  In practical terms what that means is that it calculates the rate of change in the intensity of pixels in an image.  An even more hand-wavy and pratical explanation is that calculating the Laplacian shows us where in an image the pixels change for both the X and Y directions.  OpenCV’s documentation does a good job of
explaining this
and has a great example image showing the partial derivative in the X direction, the Y direction, and both.
Doing the same thing with the data I have on hand takes just a few lines, including plotting the result.

is used to set the limits of the color mapping and enhance the contrast in the resulting plot.

data.title: Valve conquered PC gaming – what comes next?
data.author: HelloUsername
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Valve的未来发展及其在PC游戏市场中的地位

不同观点：
• Valve不应上市或改变现有领导层，以避免损害PC游戏生态。
  - 支持论据：Valve未上市，能专注于用户服务而非股东利益。若Gabe Newell离任或公司上市，PC游戏将面临重大问题。
  - 例子：其他公司以利润为导向，可能破坏PC游戏。

• Valve在PC游戏存亡之际拯救了该行业，而非仅仅利用时机推出Steam。
  - 支持论据：Valve在其他大公司转向主机时坚守PC平台，并通过SteamOS和开放计算保持PC游戏活力。
  - 对比：Microsoft等公司转向主机平台，削弱了PC游戏的潜力。

• Valve应扩展SteamOS以支持更多硬件，并提供更简便的Linux桌面环境。
  - 支持论据：Windows 10用户不愿升级，一个免费且功能齐全的Linux系统能吸引更多用户。

• Valve面临的真正威胁是Microsoft等公司在游戏订阅服务上的竞争。
  - 支持论据：PC Game Pass等服务提供了大量优质游戏，且价格低廉，可能削弱Steam的市场地位。

• Valve的垄断地位虽引发担忧，但其成功源于平台的优越性和用户体验。
  - 支持论据：尽管在PC游戏市场占主导地位，但用户仍可自由选择其他平台，Valve并未完全垄断市场。

• Valve应扩展至其他媒体内容领域，以避免错失发展机会。
  - 支持论据：Steam已有硬件产品线，如Steam Deck和VR设备，进一步扩展至多媒体领域可增强其市场地位。

补充讨论：
• Valve涉及的赌博相关问题，如战利品箱和皮肤赌博，引发监管关注。
• 讨论了Epic Games Store等竞争对手的不足之处，认为其用户体验较差，难以威胁Steam。
• 有评论提及Valve创始人可能的继承问题，尽管缺乏确凿来源。
• 有观点认为游戏行业整体可能收缩，PC游戏已过巅峰期，未来发展不确定。

争议焦点：
• Valve是否应扩展业务至其他媒体内容，或保持专注于游戏领域。
• Valve的垄断地位是否对消费者有利，及其未来可能面临的竞争威胁。
• Valve是否应进一步开放其平台以支持更多硬件和软件环境。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件测试的成本、可行性、方法及自动化工具的影响

不同观点：
• cloogshicer认为，"无法测试"的真实含义是编写这些测试的成本超过了收益。他反对测试狂热者认为可测试的系统总是更容易理解的观点，并指出在进行重大重构时，系统可能会变得更难理解。他强调，需要仔细权衡是否值得进行测试。

• j_w建议，当遇到"无法测试"的系统或功能时，应尝试隔离"不可测试"的部分，以增加可测试性。通过为这些部分编写接口并进行模拟，可以避免不可测试部分影响其他可测试功能。

• testthetest提到，随着AI的发展，单元测试的成本和测试可行性的答案正在迅速变化。AI使得单元测试几乎免费，并且通过AI工具可以促进更好的编码习惯。然而，随着软件复杂性的增加，黑盒端到端测试提供了更大的信心，因为这种测试方式更贴近真实用户体验。

• devjab强调运行时断言（runtime assertions）比传统测试更好，因为它们在问题发生时处理问题，而不是试图预测潜在的失败。他希望看到更多"非开发者聚焦"的错误处理方式，以避免在实际应用中出现意外错误。

• webdevver以讽刺的语气表示，测试应该是客户的责任，暗示开发者不应完全依赖客户反馈来进行测试。

• diggan认为，讨论内容像是博客垃圾信息，实际的演示内容在一个YouTube视频链接中。

• aspenmayer提出了关于Hacker News上karma分配的伦理问题，与主要讨论主题关系不大。

• somewhereoutth认为，如果系统由机器使用，那么可以由机器测试；如果由人类使用，则必须由人类测试。

补充讨论：
• 不同观点间争议的焦点在于测试的成本与收益的权衡、AI对测试自动化的影响、以及不同测试方法（如单元测试与端到端测试）的有效性。
• testthetest和devjab的观点形成对比，前者强调AI带来的测试自动化和单元测试的价值，后者则更看重运行时断言和人类测试的重要性。
• j_w和cloogshicer的观点部分重叠，但j_w更关注具体的技术手段（如接口和模拟），而cloogshicer更注重宏观上的权衡和经验。
• webdevver的评论带有讽刺意味，未对测试方法提供实质性建议，而是质疑开发者对测试责任的分担。
• aspenmayer的评论与主题关系不大，但引发了对社区贡献奖励机制的讨论。

总结来看，讨论围绕软件测试的实际操作性、自动化工具的影响以及不同测试方法的适用场景展开，各方观点在测试成本、收益和实施细节上存在分歧。

data.title: "Swiss Cheese" Failure Model
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：瑞士奶酪模型（Swiss Cheese Model）在不同领域的应用及其有效性，特别是在安全和事故预防方面的讨论。

不同观点：
• **robviren**：支持使用瑞士奶酪模型，认为该模型对核电站反应堆维护中的安全措施有很好的解释作用。每个核电站都要求培训该模型，强调多层防御机制的重要性，即使每个缓解措施单独看可能很傻，但整体上有效。

• **pstadler**：指出该模型也被应用于航空安全领域，并提到YouTube上的Mentour Pilot频道经常引用此模型，特别是在现有系统和程序无法防止事故发生时，强调模型在不同行业的通用性。

• **joeatwork**：对模型的长期有效性提出质疑，认为增加冗余的安全系统和深度防御可能会导致“漏洞”难以察觉，系统的复杂性增加后，这些漏洞可能会在某一天对齐并导致严重事故。强调系统复杂性对模型有效性的影响。

• **shelajev**：对链接的内容表示不满，认为维基百科上的解释更好。指出模型在思考失败预防时的价值，并以切尔诺贝利事故为例，说明多个层面的失败叠加如何导致灾难。

• **findthewords**：提到灾难通常在三件事同时出错时发生，暗示瑞士奶酪模型在解释事故多因性方面的有效性。

• **webdevver**：偏好“salami战术”，暗示对瑞士奶酪模型有不同的安全策略偏好，虽然没有详细解释该战术的具体内容。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及瑞士奶酪模型的具体应用案例，如核电站和航空安全，并提及切尔诺贝利事故作为经典失败案例。
• 对模型的有效性存在争议，一方认为它对安全防御机制有很好的解释力，另一方则质疑其在复杂系统中的长期有效性。
• 不同的安全策略偏好也在讨论中有所体现，如“salami战术”与瑞士奶酪模型的对比。

data.title: New study offers clues about what makes someone cool
data.author: _tk_
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：酷的概念及其在社会中的表现和价值

不同观点：
• glimshe认为，酷的人与研究酷的人之间交集很少，暗示研究酷并不能让人变得酷。
• neuroplots指出，资源和机会往往流向最不需要它们的人，高社交地位来源于对他人无所求，酷的本质在于不在乎，因为永远不需要在乎。
• voiper1引用了一个对酷人的特质的描述，包括外向、享乐主义、权力、冒险、开放和自主。
• whall6认为，通过学术论文来研究如何变得酷本身就不酷。
• neom认为，酷的人通常能提供灵感或洞见，酷是一种 aspirational（令人向往的）特质，并且与文化修养有关，具体特质与 voiper1 的观点相符。他还提到酷在不同文化和行业中有不同的表现。
• chriscrisby以幽默的方式表达，不用看就知道内容是显而易见的。
• webdevver分享了个人经历，从认为编程能力酷到只关注金钱，暗示价值观的转变。
• jaybrendansmith强调谦逊是永远的酷，真正酷的人不需要谈论它。
• sitkack引用The Rock的话，认为人可以有趣或酷，但不能同时兼具。
• rriley将酷与一种地位柔术联系起来，认为越少需求，越多人想要你。
• BMc2020详细说明了酷人的特质，并提出酷在建立社会等级和改变社会文化实践及规范中的作用。
• tomcam以幽默方式回应，表示显然不需要点击链接就知道内容。

补充讨论：
- 酷的定义和特质在不同评论中有所不同，但普遍提到外向、自主、冒险等特质。
- 争议的焦点在于是否可以通过研究或努力变得酷，部分评论认为酷是一种自然特质，而不是通过学术或刻意追求获得的。
- 酷与社会地位和资源的关系也是讨论的一个重点，neuroplots和rriley都提到无所求与酷之间的联系。
- 幽默和自嘲在评论中也被用作讨论酷的一种方式，增加了讨论的趣味性。

data.title: Ask HN: If AGI were invented tomorrow which countries would fare better?
data.author: mattigames
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：各国在获得AGI（人工通用智能）优势后的可能发展及其影响

不同观点：
• **jrank**：在讨论AGI的影响前，首先要考虑国家变强后会做什么。拥有AGI优势的国家可能会利用它来阻止其他国家获得AGI，并通过AGI指导获取资源以增强自身实力。对AGI应抱有希望但也要做最坏打算，尽管最坏的情况难以想象。

• **cwillu**：目前在解决对齐问题（alignment problem）上几乎没有进展。我们无法对企业或大型语言模型（LLMs）进行有效对齐控制，主流观点认为AGI不会做愚蠢的事情。拥有强大主权财富基金和完善社会项目的国家可能生存更久，但经济上被排斥是不可避免的，即使是缓慢的技术发展也会导致这种结果。

• **csomar**：讨论假设是否所有国家同时拥有AGI。如果是，则取决于各国政府的决策。如果所有国家都实施AGI的建议，资源丰富和人口众多的国家将表现良好。例如，印度尼西亚会变得富裕，而瑞士相对会变穷。实际情况有很多变量，率先达到AGI的国家有巨大优势。

• **4ad**：难以判断哪个国家会表现最好，但很明显有些国家会表现最差。欧盟会因监管使AGI失去作用，许多公民因气候变化等问题不愿使用AGI。贫困国家和弱民主国家可能会在AGI下表现良好，而民主制度可能无法在AGI下存续，除了美国。

• **bryanrasmussen**：质疑AGI是否会接管政府。当前政府领导人愚蠢的国家可能会领先。

• **neximo64**：拥有丰富且不间断能源的国家会表现更好。

• **webdevver**：AGI可能会使富国更富，穷国更穷。

• **cranberryturkey**：AI可能会先取代 offshore 工作，因此这些国家可能会表现更差。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于各国拥有AGI的先后顺序和其资源、政府决策对结果的影响。
• 对于AGI对不同类型国家（如资源丰富与贫穷国家、民主与非民主国家）的影响，存在不同看法。
• 讨论中多次提及AGI对经济和政治结构的潜在颠覆性影响。

data.title: Ask HN: What old or outdated software have you never found a replacement for?
data.author: prisenco
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对已停用或过时软件的怀念与不满，以及替代品的讨论

不同观点：
• [dradra67] 认为Apple Aperture停用对其造成很大影响，不再愿意使用专有软件管理数字收藏，目前使用DarkTable，但尚未完全替代Aperture。
• [kingkongjaffa] 怀念Command and Conquer游戏系列，特别是3 Tiberium Wars，认为其玩法（如基地建设、资源收集等）在现代没有替代品。
• [austin-cheney] 提到自己多年前停止维护的一个应用仍然有大量使用量，暗示一些老旧软件仍有实用价值。
• [mikewarot] 对Google接手后的Picassa不满，因其存在bug（随机交换面部标签）而无法使用。
• [EdwardCoffin] 提到一个已停用的电影联动应用Inception the App，展示了对独特软件消失的惋惜。
• [FerkiHN] 喜欢使用Open Office制作演示文稿，认为其无广告、无订阅且习惯使用，尽管有其他替代品。
• [aleksjess] 指出有许多库可以实现其所需功能，但这些库大多已不再更新。

补充讨论：
• [FrojoS] 怀念Skype的国际VoIP电话服务，认为其价格低廉。
• [Metalnem] 提到ClickRepair这个已停用的软件，提供档案链接。
• [j-krieger] 认为MacOS上缺乏能够有效调整不同应用音量的现代工具。
• [torunar] 提到X11这个图形用户界面标准，未具体评价。
• [delduca] 怀念Turbo C与conio.h，暗示对旧开发环境的怀念。
• [fat_cantor] 提到Dark Sky这个应用，未具体评价。
• [dogman1050] 认为Winamp的经典皮肤虽老但不过时，展示了对经典界面的喜爱。
• [lproven] 强调大纲工具对长篇写作的重要性，认为现代工具不如20-30年前的MS Word二进制文件有效，批评现代工具的简陋。

争议焦点：
• 专有软件停用对用户的影响与用户是否应再次投入精力使用新软件。
• 老旧软件的实用价值与现代替代品的不足。

总结：评论中用户普遍对已停用或过时的软件表示怀念，并对现代替代品表示不满，反映出对软件长期支持和替代方案的关注。

data.title: MI5’s falsehoods in the case of neo-Nazi spy who abused women
data.author: _tk_
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了英国安全局MI5在一宗涉及新纳粹间谍虐待女性的案件中，向法院提供虚假证据，并在之后试图掩盖事实。这名间谍X既是极端分子又是MI5线人，曾暴力虐待其女友，并威胁杀害其前伴侣的孩子。MI5最初否认X的暴力行为，并在多次法庭审理中试图保密其身份，甚至在向法院道歉后仍继续提供误导性证据。MI5进行了两次调查，但结果被认为不充分，法院命令重新调查。文章揭示了MI5内部在应对这一危机时的混乱，以及对受害人Beth的隐瞒和不公。Beth呼吁MI5公开道歉。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于MI5特工暴力事件及其后续处理的争议

不同观点：
• **vintagedave**：对MI5作为“好人”的形象感到动摇，认为MI5等机构应代表正义，但文章中的视频证据和撤诉情况令人不解，尤其是不明身份者归还证物的行为让人感到不安。
  
• **greatgib**：指出许多“民主”国家的秘密机构常为了自身利益违反法律而无需承担后果，例如某北欧国家的情报部门未经批准与美国分享国家秘密信息。这种行为表明秘密机构滥用权力，令人担忧。

• **throwawayffffas**：认为此事件反映了MI5内部的文化和领导失败，包庇不良成员只会损害整个机构的形象。引用了剑桥五人的例子，强调这种包庇行为在历史上也曾发生过。

• **fn-mote**：认为此事件表明在调查国家权力机构时需格外小心，建议对一切进行详细记录并督促政府说出真相。

• **olelele**：提到德国也曾发生类似事件，如警方线人利用告密所得资金支持右翼组织。认为秘密机构的存在本身与民主相悖，并举例英国卧底警察在环保组织中生育子女的案例。

• **wiradikusuma**：联想到“黑包”行动，对国家权力滥用的现象感到不安，尤其是低级别人员也能拥有的绝对权力。

• **diggan**：质疑MI5为何要包庇一个被描述为暴力、虐待和利用职位进行胁迫的人，认为这种行为只是为了避免对机构形象的损害，而非基于任何更有意义的理由。

• **sofixa**：虽然对事件本身感到担忧，但对BBC作为国有媒体敢于调查和报道政府机构的丑闻表示欣慰，认为这与主流媒体通常被视为共谋的叙事相悖。

补充讨论：
• **aspenmayer** 和 **wizzwizz4**：对文章标题提出修改建议，使之更直接和简明，如“MI5在涉及虐待女性的间谍案件中撒谎”。

争议焦点：
• 主要围绕MI5在处理内部不良成员时的透明度和公正性，特别是包庇行为是否为了维护机构形象而牺牲了正义。
• 对秘密机构在民主国家中的角色和行为规范的质疑，以及媒体在揭露政府丑闻中的作用。

44479029.article_content:
How MI5 piled falsehood on falsehood in the case of neo-Nazi spy who abused women
7 hours ago
Share
Save
Daniel De Simone
Investigations correspondent
•
DdesimoneDaniel
Share
Save
PA Media/BBC
When the BBC revealed that MI5 had lied to three courts, the Security Service apologised for giving false evidence - vowing to investigate and explain how such a serious failure had occurred.
But on Wednesday, the High Court ruled that these inquiries were "deficient", ordering a new "robust" investigation. A panel of judges said they would consider the issue of contempt of court proceedings against individuals once that was complete.
Now we can detail how, over the past few months leading up to the judgment, MI5 continued to provide misleading evidence and tried to keep damning material secret.
The material gives an unprecedented insight into the internal chaos at MI5 as it responded to what has become a major crisis and test of its credibility.
At the heart of the case is the violent abuse of a woman by a state agent under MI5's control. After the BBC began investigating, MI5 attempted to cover its tracks - scattering a trail of false and misleading evidence.
The case started very simply: I was investigating a neo-Nazi, who I came to understand was also an abusive misogynist and MI5 agent.
After I contacted this man - known publicly as X - in 2020 to challenge him on his extremism, a senior MI5 officer called me up and tried to stop me running a story.
The officer said X had been working for MI5 and informing on extremists, and so it was wrong for me to say he was an extremist himself.
It was this disclosure, repeated in a series of phone calls, which the Security Service would later lie about to three courts as it attempted to keep X's role and identity shrouded in secrecy.
During the phone calls with me, MI5 denied information I had about X's violence, but I decided to spend more time investigating. What I learned was that X was a violent misogynist abuser with paedophilic tendencies who had used his MI5 role as a tool of coercion.
He had attacked his girlfriend - known publicly as "Beth" - with a machete, and abused an earlier partner, whose child he had threatened to kill. He even had cannibal fantasies about eating children.
Beth, who was terrorised and coerced by X, has called for a public apology from MI5
When I challenged both X and MI5 with our evidence, the government took me and the BBC to court in early 2022. They failed to stop the story but did win legal anonymity for X.
Arguing for secrecy in a succession of court proceedings, the Security Service told judges it had stuck to its core policy of neither confirming nor denying (NCND) informants' identities, including during conversations with me. Crucially, this stance allowed it to keep evidence secret from "Beth", who had taken MI5 to court.
The service aggressively maintained its position until I produced evidence proving it was untrue - including a recording of one of the calls with a senior MI5 officer.
Finally accepting it had provided false evidence, MI5's director general Sir Ken McCallum said: "We take our duty to provide truthful, accurate and complete information very seriously, and have offered an unreserved apology to the court."
Two investigations were commissioned: an internal MI5 disciplinary inquiry, and an external review by Sir Jonathan Jones KC, who was once the government's chief lawyer. This latter review was personally commissioned by the Home Secretary Yvette Cooper and MI5's director general.
Both of these concluded that the original false evidence was not due to dishonesty by MI5 or any of its officers. They effectively put it down to mistakes, both personal and systemic.
But these two inquiries quickly began to fall apart.
Not fair or accurate
The government initially refused to provide both reports in full to the court.
Like many cases involving MI5, this one was held partly in secret to allow the government to use evidence which it says is too sensitive to be discussed in open hearings.
Access to the secret, closed part of the case was only available to the government, the judge and security-cleared barristers known as special advocates who were representing the BBC - but who were not allowed to communicate directly with us.
The government said it would not be providing any closed evidence about the two inquiries to the judge or the special advocates.
Instead, it provided an "open" version of Sir Jonathan's external review, with apparently sensitive material edited out, and it purported to provide a full account of the internal inquiry in a witness statement by MI5's director general of strategy - known as Witness B.
Sir Jonathan wrote that he was "satisfied" that the open version was a "fair and accurate" account of his full review. Witness B, third-in-command at the Security Service, said in his statement: "I am satisfied that there is nothing in the closed material that has been excluded from the open report which prevents

data.title: A 37-year-old wanting to learn computer science
data.author: chbkall
data.article_summary: 本文是一位37岁的男性自述，他希望深入学习计算机科学，目标是掌握设计API、构建数据库、操作系统、网络、驱动程序开发等技能。他并非完全的初学者，已有一定的网页开发经验，并通过自学完成了一些项目。他的职业生涯多样，主要担任小学教师，但一直对构建东西充满热情。他计划投入未来十年甚至更长时间来学习计算机科学，并得到妻子的支持。他计划开发包括社区应用、教育工具、硬件或软件产品以及电子商务应用等多个项目，并将在未来更新学习进展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大龄转行成为软件开发者的可行性及相关建议

不同观点：
• **fn-mote**：认为不应完全放弃工作，建议通过兼职或减少工作时间来保持职业结构，同时提出需要设计项目前的学习和制定退出计划。
• **andrew_lettuce**：指出计算机科学与编程的区别，建议根据动机选择方向，并强调实际应用与理论的差异。
• **lisp2240**：对转行持悲观态度，认为大龄转行者很难通过筛选，成功者多依赖人脉。
• **klipo**：分享自身成功经验，强调内在兴趣和持续学习的重要性，并提醒注意倦怠问题。
• **reactordev**：强调年龄歧视问题，鼓励不要被年龄阻碍，继续追求兴趣。
• **delis-thumbs-7e**：分享个人成功故事，强调即使有ADHD也可以通过努力实现目标。
• **WillAdams**：推荐具体学习资源，强调系统学习和数学基础的重要性。
• **WheelsAtLarge**：建议通过研究当前职位需求来指导学习，并强调设定截止日期以避免拖延。
• **clickety_clack**：分享转行经历，强调坚持和参与行业活动的重要性，提醒转行道路艰难。
• **aryehof**：认为不需要学习计算机科学，只需学习编程和相关库即可。
• **hiAndrewQuinn**：质疑不以就业为目标却关注行业年龄歧视的逻辑。
• **suzzer99**：分享个人经历，认为37岁转行不算太晚。
• **matt3210**：建议通过解决小问题来学习编程。
• **ChrisMarshallNY**：区分计算机科学与编程，强调根据目标选择学习重点。
• **giantg2**：认为年龄歧视严重，30多岁进入初级工程师职位很难。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：大龄转行是否可行，特别是关于年龄歧视和行业准入门槛的问题。
• **学习方法**：包括系统学习、项目实践、参与行业活动等不同建议。
• **职业规划**：强调内在兴趣、设定目标和制定退出计划的重要性。
• **资源推荐**：多位评论者分享了具体的学习资源和课程。

总体来看，评论中既有成功案例的分享，也有对现实困难的警示，反映出转行成为软件开发者的复杂性和多样性。

44471190.article_content:
InitCoder
Connect
A 37-year-old wanting to learn computer science
5 July 2025
Who am I?
The title says it. I am a 37-year-old wanting to learn computer science.
But who am I really?
I am someone who has always wanted to build stuff. I am fascinated by the process of creating anything. And it gives me unbridled pure joy to have people use something I have built in a meaningful and useful way.
I am not a complete beginner in computer science. I am still a somewhat-beginner. At least I know how to hack my way to build and host a minimalistic static blog like the one you are reading. I also just recently launched a slightly (only just so) more complex website for a passion project which my wife and I run
[1]
. I designed this website on my own as well while reading the book Refactoring UI
[2]
. This took me almost 4 months.
The fact that I was able to build both these websites was also thanks to this beautiful framework
[3]
(and their well written tutorials and documentation) I accidentally discovered. So I also know how to read and understand (a lot of times) technical documentation.
My career (so far)
I have had a very non-linear career graph. I left (ran away from) home when I was 16. I was unable to take up the academic pressure of wanting to excel at school and in the competitive exams that follow it.
Since then I have worked as a waiter, in an internet café, as a sales person, in a call center and in several other odd jobs. Most of my career though is spent as a teacher - teaching Math, Science and Computers to primary students.
Most of the little I know about computers (majorly some bits of web-development) is self-taught.
The plunge
I feel the desire and the need to plunge to the depths of computer science. It is not a one or two-year plan, and it is not aimed towards landing a job as a software developer. I am okay with spending the next decade of my life trying to build some level of mastery in this domain.
I know that the field is very vast and even a decade might be a small dip - but I really want to learn how to design APIs, build databases, play around with operating systems, learn about networking, write drivers for custom built devices, design and build good custom applications for my family and community, and so much more.
I have spent most of my working days in survival mode. Finally, I have some savings which can conservatively last me at least the next 5-7 years with my current minimal lifestyle. My lovely wife (who is a psychotherapist, and who believes I have adult ADHD) is supportive of my journey, and has no qualms becoming the only breadwinner of the family.
I am mindful of the ageist tendencies in the tech industry - but that does not deter me from taking this plunge - at least for now. I am also aware of some of the very good resources which are available to get me started on this path
[4]
.
What would I like to build?
Several things.
Some of these would be:
A HN / reddit themed app for the community my wife and I are building.
A device through which I can stream movies, tv serials from my device to my parents’ television - so that we can watch them together.
Education apps that leverage learning theories, community learning and game design to make learning more inspiring and accessible for students.
A product (hardware or software) that solves either a niche or a common problem - and around which I can build some kind of revenue model to sustain myself.
An e-commerce app for the wooden toys I design and document.
[5]
I am sure that some of these ideas will evolve and refine themselves over time.
Wish me all the luck for the journey I am undertaking! I will keep you updated on the progress I am making.
Notes
A community of adults which reads and uses children’s picture books as a medium to talk about complex psychological, social and emotional issues. (
https://childrensbookforall.org
)
A crash course on UI design written by founders of TailWindCSS (
https://www.refactoringui.com/
)
Astro - a JavaScript web framework optimized for building fast, content-driven websites. (
https://astro.build/
)
TeachYourselfCS (
https://teachyourselfcs.com/
) and the Computer Science curriculum of OSSU (
https://github.com/ossu/computer-science
)
Not in public domain yet, but I plan to put them in the public domain.

data.title: The Moat of Low Status
data.author: jger15
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何应对在学习新事物或追求高地位过程中可能遇到的尴尬、失败和社会压力。

不同观点：
• **高地位特权**：AceJohnny2认为高地位的人有能力承担社会风险，例如提出“愚蠢”的问题而不担心职业影响，因为他们具备更高的社会资本。
• **练习与失败的重要性**：caseysoftware强调通过实践来提高技能，并教育孩子接受失败作为成长的一部分，这种心态有助于面对失败并继续前进。
• **幸存者偏差**：andy99指出，许多人在尝试新事物时可能会遭遇失败、羞辱或拒绝，因此仅仅勇敢面对是不够的，更重要的是培养抗压能力和韧性。
• **理论与实践的平衡**：ants_everywhere认为理论学习与实践同样重要，过度强调实践而忽视理论学习可能导致错误的学习方式。
• **约束中的创造力**：k__提出在学习新事物时，利用已有知识和自我设限可以产生有趣且有效的结果，避免因为不成熟技能导致的尴尬。
• **心理障碍与真实自我**：stego-tech分享了在追求真实自我过程中面临的心理障碍，尤其是对于神经发散者，克服这些障碍是追求真实生活的关键。
• **痛苦与受苦的区别**：photon_garden指出，感受痛苦与受苦是不同的，学会感受情绪而不被其困扰可以帮助更好地应对不适。
• **低地位的祝福**：neom认为低地位并不一定是坏事，因为在这种状态下可以无畏地表达自己，最终可能带来意想不到的机会和成长。
• **年龄与社会压力**：SoftTalker认为随着年龄增长，人们会逐渐不在乎他人的看法，从而减少对尴尬和失败的担忧。
• **无混蛋区域的重要性**：ozim强调创建一个安全、无攻击性的讨论环境对于鼓励参与和分享观点至关重要。

补充讨论：
• **高地位行为的领导性**：roenxi指出，高地位的人往往通过领导行为（如首先跳舞）来引导群体行动，这种行为并非出于对低地位的恐惧，而是出于对领导地位的自信。
• **历史与讨论的关联**：FlyingSnake提到之前的相关讨论和文章，强调许多观点和策略都是基于前人经验的再创造和重新解读。

争议焦点：
• 实践中尴尬与失败的风险：部分评论者如andy99强调实践中可能遭遇的负面结果，而其他评论者如caseysoftware则更关注通过失败学习的重要性。
• 高地位与低地位的行为动机：roenxi认为高地位的人的行为更多是出于领导力的表现，而AceJohnny2则认为高地位的人有能力承担更多的社会风险。

data.title: Get the location of the ISS using DNS
data.author: 8organicbits
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种通过DNS LOC记录来获取国际空间站（ISS）位置的有趣方法。作者利用了RFC 1876实验标准，该标准允许在DNS中存储服务器的经纬度和海拔信息。作者创建了一个域名“where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io”，并通过N2YO网站的API获取ISS的实时位置数据，将其转换为LOC记录格式，定期更新。该方法使用Linux和Mac系统的`dig`命令查询ISS位置，每15分钟更新一次记录。作者还介绍了如何使用deSEC的服务来添加和更新DNS LOC记录。这种方法展示了一种复杂而有趣的方式来利用DNS存储和分发 unlikely 的数据。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过DNS记录和API获取国际空间站（ISS）位置信息的技术方法及其局限性

不同观点：
• jamesgill提供了另一个资源OpenNotify，虽然功能较少，但也可以获取ISS信息。
• kmm指出API的15分钟更新间隔过长，考虑到ISS每90分钟绕地球一圈，这会造成较大的位置误差（约地球周长的十二分之一，相当于里斯本到伊斯坦布尔的距离）。
• theobeers分享了通过DNS的NAPTR记录获取约翰逊航天中心电话号码的技术细节，提供了另一种获取相关信息的方式。
• verytrivial用幽默的方式表达了自己对长时间室内工作导致的理解误差，虽然未提出实质性观点，但反映了部分读者的感受。
• TMEHpodcast赞赏该技术的教育意义，同时提出是否可以对JWST（詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜）使用类似方法，并指出由于JWST距离过远，无法用DNS的LOC记录表示其位置，但建议可以尝试对哈勃望远镜使用类似方法。
• knadh分享了自己将该功能添加到dns.toys项目中的实践，并提供了具体使用示例。
• ritcgab从技术角度描述了DNS作为一个分布式、读优化、地理复制、最终一致性的键值存储系统的特性。
• politelemon质疑RFC中未解释为何需要DNS LOC记录，猜测可能与1996年时的大学和数据中心物流有关。
• teddyh提供了更多关于DNS LOC记录的资源链接。
• huslage提出是否可以通过实时计算星历数据来获取ISS位置，从而实现每次请求时都能获取最新位置信息。
• timzaman对"每15分钟更新一次"的速度表示惊讶。
• lordnacho询问是否存在公众可以与ISS互动的服务，并建议通过响应时间来推测ISS位置。
• xyst表示赞赏，并计划在个人DNS解析器上实现该功能。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及多个技术细节，包括DNS记录类型、API更新频率、实时计算位置的可行性等。
• 争议焦点在于API的15分钟更新间隔是否过长，以及DNS LOC记录的实际应用价值和历史背景。
• 部分评论提供了实际操作建议和资源链接，丰富了讨论的实用性。

44480223.article_content:
I love DNS esoterica. Weird little things that you can shove in the global directory to be distributed around the world instantly(ish).
Domain names, like
www.example.com
usually resolve to servers. As much as we think of "the cloud" as being some intangible morass of ethereal Turing-machines floating in probability space, the more prosaic reality is that they're just boxen in data centres. They have a physical location.
Got a tricky machine which is playing silly-buggers? Wouldn't it be nice to know exactly where it is? That way you can visit and give it some
percussive maintenance
.
Enter the DNS LOC record!
The snappily titled
RFC 1876
is an
experimental
standard. It allows you to create a DNS record which specifies the latitude and longitude of your server. Of course, some data-centres are very tall and some are underground. So it also contains an altitude parameter.
The standard allows for a minimum altitude of -100,000 metres - deep enough for any bunker! The maximum altitude is 42,849,672 metres which is high enough to allow it to be used on
satellites in geostationary orbit
.
So, as a bit of fun, I decided to create
where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io
It isn't a website. You can't ping it. There's no way to interact with it
except
by using DNS.  Yup! You can use a DNS query to get the (approximate) location of the International Space Station!
Linux and Mac users
0
can run:
dig where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io LOC
And receive back the latest position of the ISS:
;; ANSWER SECTION:
where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io. 1066 IN  LOC 47 24 53.500 N 66 12 12.070 W 430520m 10000m 10000m 10000m
The DNS records are updated every 15 minutes on a best-effort basis
1
.
How
The lovely people at
N2YO
have a website which allows you to track
loads
of objects in orbit.  They also have an
easy to use API
with a generous free tier.
Calling
https://api.n2yo.com/rest/v1/satellite/positions/25544/0/0/0/1/&apiKey=_____
gets back the latest position:
JSON
{
"info"
:
{
"satname"
:
"SPACE STATION"
,
"satid"
: 25544,
"transactionscount"
: 7
}
,
"positions"
:
[
{
"satlatitude"
: -21.25409321,
"satlongitude"
: 140.3335763,
"sataltitude"
: 420.09,
"azimuth"
: 292.92,
"elevation"
: -70.95,
"ra"
: 202.69300845,
"dec"
: -32.16097472,
"timestamp"
: 1751366048,
"eclipsed"
: true
}
]
}
Note that the altitude is in Km, whereas the LOC format requires m.
The latitude and longitude are in decimal format - they need to be converted to Degrees, Minutes, and Seconds.
There were only a few free domain name providers who offer an API for updating LOC records.  I went for
deSEC
a charity from Berlin. They have
comprehensive API documentation
.
Adding the initial LOC record is done with:
Bash
curl https://desec.io/api/v1/domains/where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io/rrsets/ \
--header "Authorization: Token _______" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" --data @- <<< \
'{"type": "LOC", "records": ["40 16 25.712 S 29 32 36.243 W 427550m 0.00m 10000m 10m"], "ttl": 900}'
However, updating the record is a little trickier. it needs to be sent as an
HTTP PATCH
to a subtly different URl. The PATCH only needs to send the data which have changed.
Bash
curl -X PATCH https://desec.io/api/v1/domains/where-is-the-iss.dedyn.io/rrsets/@/LOC/ \
--header "Authorization: Token _______" \
--header "Content-Type: application/json" --data @- <<< \
'{"records": ["40 16 25.712 S 29 32 36.243 W 427550m 0.00m 10000m 10m"]}'
I set the
Time To Live
at 900 seconds. Every 15 minutes my code runs to update the record
2
. That keeps me well within the API limits for both services.  I could add TXT records showing when it was last updated, or other sorts of unstructured data, but I think this is enough for a quick proof-of-concept.
There you have it! A complex and silly way to demonstrate how DNS can be used to hold the most unlikely of records
3
.  Say, I wonder how you'd represent the co-ordinates of the Mars Rover…?
Further Reading
For more DNS weirdness, please see my other posts:
BIMI - SVG in DNS TXT WTF?!
Why you can't dig Switzerland
I don't think there's a way for Windows users to look up LOC records using PowerShell or the Command Prompt.
↩︎
Look, I'm not NASA, OK? If you're using this to help you dock then I cannot be held responsible.
↩︎
I suppose you could build an API with unlimited request limits by distributing data via DNS TXT records. Would best suit static or infrequently updating data. Push it once to DNS and let everyone query it semi-locally.
↩︎
See if you can find the other interesting record I've added to DNS!

data.title: The War on the Walkman
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 《The Forgotten War on the Walkman》一文回顾了1979年索尼Walkman面世后引发的争议。虽然Walkman如今被视为1980年代的象征，带来怀旧情感，但其诞生之初却遭遇不少批评。文化评论家认为Walkman加剧了个人主义，导致社会隔离，甚至有人将其比作“感官抑制剂”。批评者还担心Walkman影响驾驶和行人的安全，美国多个州因此立法限制使用头戴式耳机。新泽西州Woodbridge镇甚至禁止步行过街时佩戴Walkman耳机，违者可能面临罚款和监禁。一位抗议该法律的居民Oscar Gross虽有意上诉至最高法院，但在一名耳机佩戴者发生交通事故后放弃。文章提醒人们，新技术往往面临抵制，怀旧情绪常让人忘记曾经的争议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：个人音频技术（如耳机、无线耳机）对社交互动、音乐体验以及公共安全的影响

不同观点：
• **支持个人音频设备的观点**：  
  - [comrade1234] 认为流媒体和DJ的音乐策展提供了丰富的音乐选择，且没有必要回到过去"拥有"音乐的时代。人类策展的音乐比算法推荐的更具多样性。

• **反对个人音频设备的观点**：  
  - [Lio] 偏好戴耳机的人的安静，而不是播放低质量音乐或使用自动调音的视频内容的人制造的噪音，认为这种音乐令人不适。
  - [MarkusWandel] 指出智能手机和无线耳机的普及导致人们忽视周围环境，甚至在公共道路上不注意他人的存在，增加了危险。
  - [deadbabe] 批评现代社会对人的关心减少，变得更交易性，只在对自己有利时才表现出同情。

• **对新技术影响的反思**：  
  - [sevensor] 提出个人耳机可能导致人与人之间的疏远，使得与陌生人交谈变得更加困难，类似于社会疏离的表现。

• **对公共安全的关注**：  
  - [gwern] 提到与耳机相关的公共安全事故，例如有人在过马路时因戴耳机而发生悲剧，指出这是自由的不可避免的代价。

- **怀旧情绪**：

  - [tom89999] 指出智能手机导致更多分心，包括听音乐时被电话和社交媒体打断，认为这会影响人的专注力和社交质量。

🗓️  On this day in 1979 the Sony Walkman was first released, marking its 46th anniversary
The Sony Walkman is now an icon of the 1980s, eliciting nostalgia for the ‘good old days’ of owning music, rather than renting it. Affection for the device is now universal, but that wasn’t always the case…
The sudden rise of headphone wearing pedestrians - spurred by Sony’s lightweight headsets (17% the weight of others) - caused unease about an unfamiliar new world quickly coming into view.
Some said it was a sign of a continued rise of Reagan and Thatcher style individualism. Cultural critic Allan Bloom deemed the Walkman
"a nonstop... masturbational fantasy”
in his 1987 book ‘The Closing of the American Mind.’ Neo-Luddite John Zerzan saw the Walkman as part of a modern trend that encouraged a
"protective sort of withdrawal from social connections"
and Thomas Lipscomb, chief of the Center for the Digital Future, equated it with the euphoric drug "soma," from Huxley's Brave New World, creating, as he put it,
"an airtight bubble of sound"
that was nothing but a
"sensory depressant."
In other words it all felt ‘a bit blackmirror’ as one might say today.
(A collection of quotes collected in this 1999 Reason Magazine
article
)
The Walkman, critics claimed, was more than just music to one's ears; it was a tool of societal disconnect and for government officials and law enforcement a danger on the roads, because it limited the hearing of drivers, cyclists and pedestrians.
After a number of accidents involving Walkman headphones, numerous states across the US swiftly put into effect or proposed restrictions, many related to headphone use while driving or cycling. Among them were statutes in California, Florida, Georgia, , Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and Washington.
The New Jersey township of Woodbridge went a step further, forbidding not just driving or biking, but even crossing the street while wearing Walkman headphones.
The price for breaking this prohibition? A potential two-week stay in jail and a fine. The law made national and international news, including the BBC who got reactions on the street:
The day the law was put into effect - Oscar Gross - a retiree from a neighbouring town, was spurred into action. Seething, he approached Police Sergeant Lou Monzo, purposefully donned his headphones, and crossed the street.
The outcome of this small act of civil disobedience? Gross became the first person to receive a citation for wearing headphones (even though they weren’t plugged into anything.) Undeterred, he stated in an interview,
"I’m prepared to go to jail for 15 days just to prove a point."
Gross end up being interviewed for national outlets as did members of the Woodbridge town council. However, to his disappointment, Gross was not sent to jail. After the judge imposed a $50 fine, which was later suspended, a frustrated Gross said to a journalist:
"He didn't even give me the opportunity to say that I was willing to serve time in jail."
"No municipality has the right to tell somebody what they can wear." -
Oscar Gross
Oscar Gross was
preparing
to take the case all the way to the supreme court, but backed out after someone was killed crossing the street while wearing headphones. The kind of tragic anecdote that is the inevitable and unavoidable price of freedom.
This chapter in techno-pessimism is a good reminder that nostalgia tends to elicit amnesia about the resistance new technologies once faced. After all, who would have thought the “good old days” could ever have been considered a bad, brave new world?

data.title: Stop killing games and the industry response
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了一项名为“停止毁坏电子游戏”的欧洲公民倡议，该倡议已获得超过100万个签名。其目标是要求游戏发行商确保售出的游戏在功能上保持可玩状态，防止发行商通过远程停用游戏。该倡议特别关注单人游戏，即使在线服务终止，游戏也应可继续运行。这一倡议由YouTube创作者Accursed Farms发起，他以游戏《The Crew》为例说明了问题。游戏由于依赖于发行商的服务器，一旦服务终止，游戏即无法游玩，尽管玩家最初以为他们购买了游戏。

文章批评了这种“租赁”模式，并建议对在线游戏应明确标识为订阅服务，而对于单人游戏，即使没有网络连接也应保持可玩。游戏行业对此作出回应，表示停止在线服务是复杂的商业决策，需保持这一选项以应对商业不可行的情况。文章作者对此持批评态度，认为没有正当理由无法保证游戏的可玩性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏行业的商业模式、法律监管以及玩家权利

不同观点：
• **calibas 的观点**：游戏发行商希望通过不断推出新内容和微交易来迫使玩家持续消费，而不是制作像《Terraria》这样耐玩的游戏。他们倾向于让游戏的生命周期更短，以推动玩家购买更多新游戏和附加内容。

• **bellgrove 的观点**：一些公司如Ubisoft，过于注重复制成功的游戏模式，而不是鼓励创新。这导致了许多游戏缺乏深度，只是为了消耗玩家时间。

• **throw10920 的观点**：对即将出台的法律表示担忧。虽然法律的初衷可能是好的，但实施过程中可能会被腐败或技术 incompetence 所影响，导致不合理负担或无效监管。

• **umvi 的观点**：消费者可以通过选择不购买有问题的游戏来表达不满。市场上有许多不采用“不正当”商业模式的游戏。

• **izzydata 的观点**：提议在购买时明确游戏的服务年限，这样消费者可以做出更明智的选择。目前，游戏发行商可以在很短的时间内关闭游戏服务，这是不合理的。

• **layer8 的观点**：如果立法通过，可能会导致“终身订阅”模式的普及，而这并不能真正解决问题，只是改变了付费方式。

• **PoshBreeze 的观点**：对游戏公司关于私人服务器的论点表示不满，认为这些论点充满了误导。玩家运营私人服务器不应让公司承担责任。

• **fidotron 的观点**：强调了游戏行业中涉及的复杂IP和许可问题，指出这些问题使得一些提议不切实际。

• **benoau 的观点**：批评游戏公司希望完全自主决定游戏命运，而不考虑消费者权利。这导致了许多游戏历史因在线依赖和市场规则而消失。

• **mopsi 的观点**：问题不仅限于游戏行业，还涉及到越来越多的依赖于制造商服务的智能设备。建议通过法律要求开放本地API以减少电子废物。

• **subjectsigma 的观点**：如果立法通过，大型游戏公司可能会将新游戏重新标记为“订阅”模式或停止制作单人游戏，最终可能不会有实质性改变。玩家可以选择不购买这些公司的游戏。

• **dandersch 的观点**：对开发者对该倡议的支持不足感到困惑。认为开发者应更积极地捍卫自己的工作成果，而不是仅仅因为法律约束而退缩。

补充讨论：

44480284.article_content:
Stop killing games and the industry response
Date:
2025-06-06
Recently, there's been a
European Citizens' Initiative called "Stop Destroying Videogames"
which by now has hit the milestone of 1'000'000 signatures. You're still encouraged to sign it if you care about its goals and are a EU citizen, since not all of those are likely to be valid signatures, but overall this is a pretty positive trend:
If it does indeed get enough valid signatures, it will
get passed on to the European Commission
and new laws might get passed as a consequence. However, there has been some opposition to it, so today I'd like to briefly describe what it's about, as well as why some of the people disagree with it, and why they might be quite wrong in doing so.
Why are video games being killed
First up, the actual objectives are pretty concise, here they are:
This initiative calls to require publishers that sell or license videogames to consumers in the European Union (or related features and assets sold for videogames they operate) to leave said videogames in a functional (playable) state.
Specifically, the initiative seeks to prevent the remote disabling of videogames by the publishers, before providing reasonable means to continue functioning of said videogames without the involvement from the side of the publisher.
The initiative does not seek to acquire ownership of said videogames, associated intellectual rights or monetization rights, neither does it expect the publisher to provide resources for the said videogame once they discontinue it while leaving it in a reasonably functional (playable) state.
It was all more or less kicked off by
a YouTube creator named Accursed Farms
, who illustrated why this matters with the example of the game
The Crew
:
So what does this mean on a practical level?
Suppose you bought a game like The Crew back when it came out, in 2014. The game is about racing around in cars and can be played both in singleplayer modes and multiplayer modes, with other players. However, the game is made in such a way, that the account management functionality depends on servers, hosted by Ubisoft. This means that once some time passes and supporting those servers is no longer viable (once that AWS bill starts racking up and there are no new sales), Ubisoft is going to turn them off, just like they did in 2024, making the game unplayable.
Even the singleplayer components: you just wanting to race around cars in a world with you and other NPCs in it, is no longer viable. Essentially, you didn't "buy" the game, but in a sense were "renting" it for an indeterminate amount of time, a lease that expired due to the publishers and developers no longer wanting to provide that service for you. Yet, it wasn't marketed to you as a subscription, you thought that you were buying something, but were instead just being misled.
I don't think that's acceptable, not even remotely. Objectively, there are also no good reasons (there are reasons, just not good ones) for things to be that way: singleplayer games in general have been around for decades. If Need for Speed 2: SE could do that back in 1996 (which was my first racing game that I played years and years after its initial release on my dad's old work laptop), then surely there's no good reason for the comparably huge corporations of the current day and age to be unable to do so either:
To sum up what I think should happen, is being upfront when a game is online only and calling it a subscription, something that would be relatively easy to implement (and is often already supported) in all online stores. You don't have to re-architect your entire game if you don't want to say that you are letting people buy it. You can just call it what it is, a subscription.
Similarly, you can sell a singleplayer game with optional multiplayer components: if I have a PC with no Internet connection and if it stayed that way for a decade, the singleplayer components should still work. On the other hand, if you want to sell a game that would otherwise be online only, you need to make it so that once you end your support for it, there must be a way for people to keep playing what they bought. I'll get into some of the ways how to do that later.
That's it. But clearly there's lots of pushback.
The industry response
Once the initiative reached its initial signature goal, there was
a statement released by Video Games Europe
, an association of a bunch of video game publishers in Europe. First up, it's cool that organizations like that exist, that there's a decent video game industry in the EU as well and some organization around the craft. Secondly, I don't quite agree with the statement, but understand their concerns.
So here it is:
We appreciate the passion of our community; however, the decision to discontinue online services is multi-faceted, never taken lightly and must be an option for companies when an online experience is no longer commercially viable. We understand that it can be disappointing

文章主要讨论了一项名为“停止毁坏电子游戏”的欧洲公民倡议，该倡议已获得超过100万个签名。其目标是要求游戏发行商确保售出的游戏在功能上保持可玩状态，防止发行商通过远程停用游戏。该倡议特别关注单人游戏，即使在线服务终止，游戏也应可继续运行。这一倡议由YouTube创作者Accursed Farms发起，他以游戏《The Crew》为例说明了问题。游戏由于依赖于发行商的服务器，一旦服务终止，游戏即无法游玩，尽管玩家最初以为他们购买了游戏。

文章批评了这种“租赁”模式，并建议对在线游戏应明确标识为订阅服务，而对于单人游戏，即使没有网络连接也应保持可玩。游戏行业对此作出回应，表示停止在线服务是复杂的商业决策，需保持这一选项以应对商业不可行的情况。文章作者对此持批评态度，认为没有正当理由无法保证游戏的可玩性。

data.title: Two and a Half Years in GameDev
data.author: _sJiff
data.article_summary:
本文作者分享了从传统企业开发转向游戏开发（GameDev）行业的经历和观察。尽管作者在加入游戏公司前没有相关经验，但在三年内通过与业内人士交流，逐渐了解了该行业的独特之处。文章主要观点包括：

1. **热情驱动**：游戏行业特别强调对游戏的热情。与传统IT行业不同，这里的人们非常关注游戏动态，讨论行业新闻和产品细节。虽然也可以在不热衷游戏的情况下从事某些岗位，但融入游戏文化更有助于职业发展。

2. **创意至上**：游戏开发高度注重创意，与企业开发的结构化流程形成鲜明对比。创意在游戏设计和开发中占据核心地位，影响着团队的工作方式和项目推进。

3. **多样化角色**：尽管游戏行业需要各种技术角色，但对游戏的热爱仍然是普遍的职业驱动力。即便某些岗位不直接涉及游戏内容，了解游戏文化仍然有助于更好地协作和工作。

总的来说，游戏开发行业独特的工作文化和创意氛围使其与传统开发工作形成鲜明对比。
